*.text: Florida has no grid operator. Each utility files a Ten-Year Site Plan every April with the Public Service Commission (PDFs at floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/<year>/<Utility>.pdf, open with curl). A plan's retirement year is a target, not a decision, and is marked approximate: stage Planned retire from a plan only when the plan gives a month and year and the plan is the current one. Projects of 75 MW and above need a need determination from the commission (filings at floridapsc.com/library/filings/<year>/<number>/<number>.pdf).

L100001048250.text: JEA Power Island power station unit 1 is pre-construction at 700 MW with EIP identifiers only. The Public Service Commission found need in August 2026 (Docket 20260087-EM) for a 675 MW combined cycle unit on the former St. Johns River Power Park site, $1.57 billion, planned for 2031 (News4Jax and Hoodline, August 2026; the commission's order in the docket). Stage Capacity (MW) 675 and Start year 2031 if the order or JEA states them, add a Status Detail line at the top with the need finding and its link, and add 'St. Johns River Power Park Unit 3' to Other Name(s) if JEA uses that name. The possible-updates sheet says the record should be combined into St. Johns River Power Park; put that in a question, do not merge.

L100000401632.text: Florida Power and Light agreed on August 20, 2025 to buy the Vandolah plant from Northern Star, FERC approved in December 2025, and the plant is to serve the company from June 1, 2027. Stage Owner(s) only if a source says the sale closed. If it is still pending, leave Owner(s) alone and put what you found in a question.

L100000103824.text: Florida Power and Light's 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan (investor.nexteraenergy.com, FPL 2026-2035 TYSP PDF) says Gulf Clean Energy Center units 4 and 5 (the converted 93.7 MW gas rows 'tp2') retire at the end of 2029. Stage Planned retire 2029 on the gas rows if the plan gives the date, and add a Status Detail line at the top.

L100000103829.text: The 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan says Lansing Smith CT 3A (about 40 MW, oil) retires in the fourth quarter of 2027. GEM has CT1 at 41.8 MW oil. Confirm the GEM unit is the same turbine and stage Planned retire 2027 on it if the plan gives the date.

L100000409200.text: Duke Energy Florida's 2025 Ten-Year Site Plan retires Bayboro P1 to P4 in September 2026. The August 2026 EIA-860M table lists P3 as retired in 2025. Check Duke's 2026 plan for the current date. If the units have retired, stage Status retired and Retired year with two independent publishers; if the date is still in the future, stage Planned retire 2026.

L100000401871.text: Duke's 2025 plan retires P L Bartow peakers P1 and P3 in June 2027 and P2 and P4 in June 2034. Confirm with Duke's 2026 plan and stage Planned retire per unit. GEM lists the peakers at about 75 MW while EIA gives 55.4 MW; put the capacity disagreement in a question, do not change Capacity (MW) without two agreeing sources.

L100000401867.text: Duke's 2025 plan retires DeBary peakers 2 to 6 in June 2027, while EIA-860M shows 2034 for some of them. Resolve with Duke's 2026 plan and stage Planned retire per unit from the newest plan only.

L100000401869.text: Duke's 2025 plan retires Intercession City units 1 to 6 in June 2034. Confirm with the 2026 plan and stage Planned retire 2034 on those six units only; leave the other units alone.

L100000401872.text: Duke's 2025 plan retires Suwannee River units 1 to 3 in June 2034. Confirm with the 2026 plan and stage Planned retire 2034 if it still says so.

L100000103826.text: Gainesville Regional Utilities' 2026 plan tentatively retires Deerhaven turbines 1 and 2 and the steam units in 2031, 2032 and 2036, with dates that may slip. Stage Planned retire only where the plan gives a firm year per unit; otherwise add a Status Detail line. Check the converted unit 2 gas row for a missing Start year.

L100000103820.text: Big Bend CC1 (1,241 MW) has no Start year. Stage it if Tampa Electric or EIA dates commercial operation. Tampa Electric's board approved a unit 4 modernization to combined cycle after its April 2026 plan was filed (filing 04359-2026 at floridapsc.com); the coal unit 4 is still operating. Write the modernization up as a question with the source; a new unit record is for the state-wide search, not this brief.

L100000103831.text: Polk unit 1 gasification retired at the end of 2024 and the combustion turbine is being upgraded to run on gas. Check the GEM unit 1 gas row ('tp2', 192.9 MW) status and stage Status Detail with the 2025 plan's wording. Polk unit 2 gets two 59.5 MW enhancements (November 2026 and June 2027): an uprate on an existing unit stays on the watch list, do not change Capacity (MW).

L100000103835.text: Stanton unit 1 gas row ('tp2', 464.5 MW) is cancelled in GEM: the Orlando Utilities Commission chose extended cold shutdown by the end of May 2026 instead of converting to gas. Confirm the cancellation year from the 2025 or 2026 plan and stage a Status Detail line. Stanton unit 2 gas row is announced: find whether the gas-only conversion has a date or has started, and stage Status or Start year only with sources. Do not change the owner shares without the plan's ownership table.

L100000401968.text: Osceola CTG1 is mothballed in GEM. The Orlando Utilities Commission bought the Osceola peakers in 2021. Check the 2025 or 2026 plan and EIA for whether CTG1 is back in service or retired; stage Status only with two independent publishers.

L100000402179.text: Indian River units 1 to 3 are mothballed in GEM. Check the Orlando Utilities Commission plan and EIA for whether they have been retired; stage Status retired and Retired year only with two independent publishers.

L100000407393.text: Shady Hills combined cycle G001 (573 MW, EIA 63802) is under construction in GEM. Find whether it reached commercial operation. Stage Status operating and Start year with two independent publishers; EIA-860M alone makes it a single-source status change.

L100000401950.text: Manatee CT1 and CT2 (237.5 MW each) are announced in GEM. Check whether Florida Power and Light's 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan still lists them. If the 2026 plan drops them, do not cancel on your own: add a Status Detail line and put it in a question. The plan's Manatee unit 3 upgrade for the second quarter of 2027 is a watch item, not a capacity change.

L100000401951.text: Florida Power and Light's 2026 plan lists 3,276 MW of new combustion turbines at Martin from 2032 to 2035 ('2032 4x0 Martin CTs' 932 MW, the same in 2033 and 2034, '2035 2x0 Martin CTs' 596 MW). These are not in GEM. A gas project in a plan is enough to add it: write the plan lines up as candidate new units for Martin Point with the plan's page, capacity and year, and flag them as plan-sourced. The Martin unit 3 upgrade for 2028 is a watch item.

L100001064466.text: Duke Energy IRP Power station 1 holds two announced 254.5 MW placeholder units from Duke's plan. Check Duke's 2026 Ten-Year Site Plan for the current combustion turbine additions (the 2025 plan had four turbines in 2033 and 2034). Stage Start year and a Status Detail line from the newest plan, set Latest Activity to the plan date, and flag the record as plan-sourced. The coordinates are placeholders shared with the Seminole IRP records; say so in a question.

L100001064460.text: Seminole 2025 IRP power station 1 (610 MW announced) comes from Seminole Electric Cooperative's 2025 plan (a 620 MW combined cycle in 2032). Check Seminole's 2026 plan for the current capacity and year, stage Start year and a Status Detail line from the newest plan, set Latest Activity to the plan date, and flag the record as plan-sourced. The coordinates are placeholders; say so in a question.

Check Seminole's 2026 plan for the current capacity and year, stage Start year and a Status Detail line from the newest plan, set Latest Activity to the plan date, and flag the record as plan-sourced.
